newsitem.title: USA: Harris Methodist, Texas, lists Q1 1997 results.
newsitem.headline: Harris Methodist, Texas, lists Q1 1997 results.

text.p: Harris Methodist Health System said Tuesday it earned a net excess of $8.3 million on revenues of $258.4 million for the three months ended March 31, 1997, compared to a net excess of $8.6 million on revenues of $228.7 million for the year-ago period.

Harris Methodist Health Plan, Inc., which includes the System's for-profit HMO, had net income of $2.2 million on revenues of $119.7 million for the first quarter, compared to a net income of $2.5 million on revenues of $99.5 million during the year-ago period.

"Our financial performance during the first quarter of the year reflects the continuing pressure on managed care premiums and hospital reimbursement, as the managed care penetration in North Texas grows," Ronald L. Smith, president and CEO of Harris Methodist Health System, said. "The fact that our net excess did not decline compared to a year ago really is a positive indicator."

Smith added that the growth of managed care is one reason that Harris Methodist announced in March the signing of a non-binding letter of intent with Presbyterian Healthcare Resources to create a larger, community-based, not-for-profit health create system. A larger system would be better able to provide the broad network employers demand, as well as ensuring the continued ability of both organizations to fulfill their not-for-profit missions, he said.

As of March 31, membership in the commercial and senior HMOs totaled 251,317, an increase of 9.3 percent from March 31, 1996. Additionally, membership in the six-month-old Harris Methodist STAR Plan, a Medicaid HMO, continues to grow, reaching 16,335 on March 31. Much of the HMO growth is occurring in the Senior Health Plan, which is Harris' Medicare risk product, the Individual and Family Plan, and the STAR Plan.
